caption:
He lost his hand to a falling metal sheet in 2015 and thought his javelin career was over. Then a disqualification at the Rio Paralympics nearly broke him again.

Sundar Singh Gurjar, from Karauli, Rajasthan, was already competing in javelin at the junior national level when an accident severed his hand in 2015, sending him into despair. Coach R.D. Singh introduced him to para-athletics in the F46 classification and he rebuilt his career from scratch - only to be disqualified at the Rio 2016 Paralympics after arriving 52 seconds late to the call room, a setback that reportedly required psychiatric support and help from his coach and friends to recover from. He fought back to win gold at the Para Athletics World Championships in 2017 and 2019, set an Asian record with a 68.60m throw and went on to win bronze medals at both the Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 Paralympics in the men's javelin F46 event.
